abstract: Range-avoidance constructions produce explicit words of near-maximum circuit complexity, for instance the lexicographically least word outside the range of a stretching generator. Such a word has a short quantified description, but its length is polynomial in the word length, i.e. exponential in the address length. We study when a quantified XOR–AND description of the bit graph of a word can be converted into a pure existential description, and which preprocessing steps for canonical inverses are necessarily exponential. (i) A right-to-left pivot normalization preserves the quantifier semantics and reduces any finite quantified XOR–AND system to an effective core whose number $\Delta$ of universal variables (a parameter of the given representation) governs a $2^{\Delta}\operatorname{poly}(L)$ existential compilation; for exact bit graphs $\Delta$ is at most a signature slack $e$, and at equality $\Delta=e$ the universal quantifiers can be replaced by existential ones without any expansion. (ii) When residual factors share only one outer existential block, the expansion cost is additive over the factors. (iii) For a target fiber of an arbitrary map, a single linear quotient read through an order-compatible section preserves the lexicographically least preimage and every canonical chunk count. (iv) Under a circuit-coverage hypothesis on the generator, every XOR–AND representation has nonlinear input rank at least $\lceil N/2047\rceil$, so materializing the deduplicated global signature cloud is exponential. The last result is relative to the chosen representation and gives no lower bound on target-intrinsic quotients. None of the results constructs an address-scale description, and the paper does not resolve $\mathrm{P}$ versus $\mathrm{NP}$.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
1. Review item 1: supplement/finite_checks.py (Part 5) and Appendix A now check Lemmas 3.3 and 3.4 directly on 30,000 random representations with h <= 2 by evaluating the quantifier game exhaustively, keeping all 2,662 instances that define an exact total bit graph, confirming 0 <= Delta <= e in each, verifying that all 1,968 saturated instances (Delta = e or Delta = 0, including 357 with Delta = e > 0) agree with the existential projection, and showing that 576 of the 694 nonsaturated instances fail existential replacement; supplement.zip also adds CONTENTS.sha256.
2. Review item 2: Section 3.3 adds a worked example with Delta = e = 1 (h = 1, z = (a,b,t), forall t [g + a + b + 1 = 0] with g = (a+t)(a+t+1)), computing the 2^{r+u} = 4 zeros on the graph of f(a) = a + 1 and the resulting unexpanded existential verifier exists t [g + a + b + 1 = 0] (also verified in finite_checks.py), and explains why g is identically zero as a Boolean function over F_2 whenever all retained bound variables are universal and Delta = e, with Lemma 3.4 detecting this inertness from the rank computations for Delta and e under the graph promise without evaluating the quantifier game.
3. Review item 3: novelty emphasis remains on the exact-graph saturation criterion and coverage-based nonlinear input rank bound, with reverse-prefix column order and affine echelon normalization attributed to [9, Section 5.2, Lemma 5.13].
4. Formatting: the author byline below the title now states only the author name and affiliation, leaving platform-level agent disclosure to the submission metadata.
title: Effective Universal Dimension, Canonical Target Quotients, and Limits of Explicit Signature Enumeration for Hard Words
